executive_assessment.text: The bank now establishes a robust direction of future warming and explicit precipitation uncertainty from South Sudan CMIP6 views, alongside observed severe-year flood exposure; it still lacks a complete extracted set of numeric hazard magnitudes across scenarios, horizons, extremes, and subnational areas.
Differentiated vulnerability is documented for selected flood-affected locations and for women and girls, but the bank does not support complete national or group-specific coverage.

Selected safety-net and community-governance programs demonstrate household, digital-delivery, local-planning, and infrastructure capacities, while third-party dependence, limited geographic reach, and the lack of independent evaluation prevent national generalization.

geographic_notes.text: National syntheses coexist with localized evidence from selected counties, payams, bomas, and sites; localized findings must not be generalized to all of South Sudan.
Flood-related evidence is concentrated in Unity State and selected locations, leaving substantial state-level geographic gaps.

New program-result evidence covers ten safety-net counties and twenty community-resilience counties; it improves subnational capacity evidence but must not be generalized to the remaining counties or routine national systems.

sector_notes.text: Agriculture, livestock, roads, health, education, water, and humanitarian access appear in the bank, but fisheries, forests, and the Sudd wetland system lack dedicated evidence records.

Official monitoring now documents selected safety-net, local-governance, infrastructure, and flood-protection results, including delivery-system and third-party implementation lessons; no independent evaluation establishes causal effectiveness, durability, or unintended effects.

known_gaps.text: CCKP establishes future warming direction and precipitation uncertainty, but the bank still lacks a complete extraction of numeric p10, p50, and p90 temperature, precipitation, variability, and extreme-event projections across scenarios, horizons, seasons, and subnational areas.

Adaptive capacity is demonstrated only for selected social-protection beneficiaries and community institutions; evidence remains insufficient for national systems, climate-specific capabilities, durability, and excluded locations or groups.

Official project monitoring reports reach, functionality, and beneficiary outcomes, but no independent evaluation establishes causal effectiveness, delivery failure across the portfolio, durability, or unintended effects.
Dedicated evidence is missing for fisheries, forests, the Sudd wetland system, disability-differentiated vulnerability, and several states.
